business_scope.primary_industry_name: Computer Vision Bounding-Box Annotation and RLHF Data Curation

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Independent State of Samoa (International Companies regime administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law inherited from colonial tradition, with limited customary law overlay; statutory framework modeled on commonwealth corporate law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No comprehensive BIT with the PRC; case-by-case

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 5 (Incorporation), 10 (Memorandum and Articles of Association), 12 (Effect of Certificate of Incorporation), 28 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 39 (Directors); read together with the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2011 and the International Companies Regulations 1998.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon electronic submission of the Memorandum and Articles of Association together with the Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1) through a SIFA-licensed registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; share capital may be expressed in any currency and is subscribed at such par value as the subscribers determine. No escrow account or bank deposit requirement is imposed under Samoan law for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that: (1) the subscription for the issued shares of the Company as recorded in the share register is hereby approved and the Directors are directed to issue the corresponding share certificates; (2) the registered office at Level 2, SIFA Centre, Apia, Samoa is adopted as the Company's statutory registered office and the SIFA-licensed registered agent is retained; (3) [Director Name], [Secretary Name], and [Authorized Representative Name] are appointed to their respective offices with full authority to execute all filings, open bank or payment accounts (including PayPal and Wise), and bind the Company; (4) the Directors shall complete all post-incorporation registrations and procure the tax exemption certificate. Any one officer may act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) via a licensed international company agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed company names ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' through the SIFA-licensed agent. The agent conducts a name availability search against the SIFA register and reserves the approved name for a period of 30 days. Provide written consent from the shareholder or director for use of the name prior to reservation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form (agent-prepared)
Notarized copy of passport of the intended shareholder and director
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association stating the proposed name
Confirmation of non-resident ownership status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or prohibited character, resubmit with an alternative name or file an administrative appeal to the Registrar with a written submission within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Samoa or in the jurisdiction of the subscriber (document may be notarized abroad), with authentication for Samoan registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association in the presence of a notary public. The notary must witness the subscriber's signature and affix a notarial certificate. If executed outside Samoa, attach a certificate of authentication (Apostille) under the 1961 Hague Convention. Deliver the notarized set to the SIFA-licensed registered agent for filing.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (2 original executed counterparts)
Notarial certificate of execution
Apostille or consular authentication (for foreign-executed documents)
Consent to act as director and shareholder from each appointed person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to notarization or wording, the agent will return the document for execution correction; no fresh filing fee is charged where the objection is raised within the initial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registrar of International Companies (electronic lodgment through licensed agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent lodges the Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1) together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles, the registered office consent, registered agent consent, and a statutory declaration of compliance. The application is submitted via the SIFA e-registry portal and receipted with a unique filing reference.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation (signed by agent)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (notarized set)
Consent to act as registered agent (Form IC-2)
Consent to use registered office address (Form IC-3)
Certificate of good standing or identity verification of the agent (if newly licensed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar issues a query or request for further information, the agent has 21 days to provide a written response; late responses are cured by resubmission with any required correction and no penalty if made in good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Revenue and Registry Unit (treasury account of Samoa government)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The agent pays the official state incorporation fee of USD 200 (or equivalent in SAM tala) by bank transfer or from a pre-funded SIFA account. Fees comprise incorporation charge and the first annual license fee (unless the company elects an exemption later). A receipt is generated and attached to the filing record.
required_dossiers: SIFA fee invoice / pro-forma
Bank transfer confirmations or treasury receipt
Proof of agent authorization to pay
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied or fails, reconcile the transaction with SIFA's treasury section and issue a corrected payment receipt; late payment incurs a penalty of USD 50 plus 10% of the unpaid fee per month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Incorporation Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review and fee clearance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (dated as of filing). The agent then files the first board resolution, registers the directors and secretary, and prepares the company's minute book and share certificates. The company may commence business on the date of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original)
First Board Resolution (original)
Notice of directors and secretary (Form IC-4)
Registered office and agent confirmation
Share register and certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error or is withheld pending verification, apply to the Registrar for rectification within 90 days; the Registrar may issue an amended certificate upon sworn evidence without re-filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Division of Trade, Industry and Investment, Apia, Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - ISIC 8220 data labeling and AI training BPO is an unlicensed offshore professional service under Samoan law; no sectoral operating permit is required for an International Company serving non-resident clients. A standard business registration is not required where the company does not trade within Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Permitted Activity: office-based computer vision annotation and RLHF data curation with no manufacturing or industrial discharge; requires only an Environmental Registration Certificate, not a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from office sanitation discharged to Samoa Water Authority sewers meeting the Samoa Effluent Standards (BOD5 <= 50 mg/L, TSS <= 50 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0); negligible VOC emissions as no industrial solvents are used, with indoor air quality compliant with WHO guidelines (VOC < 0.5 mg/m3); e-waste from obsolete computing hardware managed under the Waste Management Act 2010 and the Basel Convention transboundary controls.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) verifying alarm, suppression, and egress compliance; structural load inspection by PUMA building control confirming floor loading for server and workstation racks; workplace certificate of compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 issued by MCIL covering ergonomic workstations, electrical safety, emergency lighting, and exit signage for the annotation operations floor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa - the national tax administration established under the Tax Administration Act 2012, succeeding the Inland Revenue Services division of the Ministry of Finance. Official e-services and TIN/VAGST registration portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws. The Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) administers incorporation and annual government fees of International Companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is statutorily tax-exempt and is not required to obtain a TIN for offshore operations. Procedure when a TIN/VAGST ID is needed for local procurement, input credit recovery, or bank onboarding: (1) file Form VAGST-01 (Registration Application) with the MfR; (2) attach certified certificate of incorporation, IC registration certificate, registered agent consent, registered office address in Samoa, director/shareholder particulars, and a business description covering AI data-labeling and RLHF BPO services; (3) the Commissioner of Revenue verifies and issues the TIN and VAGST registration certificate, effective from the application date or a later elected date (VAGST Act 2008, ss.12-16); (4) for pure offshore ICs, fiscal compliance is satisfied by payment of the annual government fee to the Registrar of International Companies, not by domestic TIN registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - the Samoa IC is a non-resident offshore vehicle exempt from income tax, VAGST, and stamp duty in respect of all offshore business and foreign-source income under s.173 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). The exemption is conditional on conducting no business with Samoa residents, holding no Samoa land, and paying the annual government fee. Breach of conditions subjects the IC to the domestic tax net: 27% corporate income tax and 15% VAGST assessed without transitional relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box election, no IC-to-resident taxation election, and no hybrid/mismatch elections under BEPS Action 2. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) voluntary VAGST registration election, including below-threshold registration, under VAGST Act 2008 s.13, which enables zero-rated exporters to reclaim input VAGST; (ii) private binding ruling application to the Commissioner under the Tax Administration Act 2012 confirming offshore BPO income classification; (iii) IC continuation or migration out of Samoa under the International Companies Act 1987 to change tax residence without liquidation; (iv) amendment of the IC's memorandum of association to expand business scope without domestic tax consequences while offshore-exempt status persists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 (Samoa Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period for compulsory VAGST registration of persons established in Samoa or with a Samoa fixed establishment; voluntary registration permitted below threshold with Commissioner approval (VAGST Act 2008, s.12). An offshore IC's exported data-labeling services are zero-rated or outside the scope of Samoa VAGST and do not trigger domestic registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government e-invoicing API, and no digital stamping requirement. Tax invoices must contain the seller and buyer names and TINs, invoice number, date, supply description, quantity, and VAGST amount in WST (VAGST Act 2008, ss.55-58). The MfR eServices portal accepts electronic VAGST return filing and payment but does not pre-clear individual invoices. Zero-rated export supplies are evidenced by commercial invoices supplemented by digital service delivery records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under VAGST Act 2008, zero-rated supplies include exported goods, exported services performed directly for a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, and services supplied in connection with goods exported from Samoa. The offshore AI data-labeling and RLHF BPO qualifies where: (a) the client is non-resident with no Samoa fixed establishment; (b) the benefit of the annotation services is consumed wholly outside Samoa; (c) delivery occurs via digital rails (MassPayPal/Wise) to offshore data platforms; (d) payment is received in foreign currency through a licensed Samoa commercial bank; and (e) contemporaneous evidence is maintained: executed master services agreement, work orders, annotation/RLHF delivery logs, dataset handover manifests, and client acceptance certificates.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Single Administrative Document (SAD) filed with the Samoa Customs Service for any physical export leg (servers, equipment, storage media); for purely digital services, substituted by the service export dossier comprising the contract, data-processing logs, and IP/annotation delivery records.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill - required only for physical goods movement; for digital BPO services, replaced by digital delivery evidence: encrypted dataset handover manifests, cloud service receipts, and signed client acceptance certificates.

Inward Remittance Certificate - certificate or SWIFT credit advice from a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency client funds; mandated by the Exchange Control Act 1976 and relied on by the MfR for zero-rating verification and input VAGST refund substantiation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The MfR may audit zero-rating claims within a 4-year reassessment window, with no limitation period where fraud or wilful evasion is proven. Fabricated export invoices, false remittance certificates, or sham offshore structures trigger: (i) denial of zero-rating with assessment of 15% VAGST and back-interest; (ii) shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 of up to 100% of tax avoided; (iii) criminal prosecution under VAGST Act 2008 with fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years; (iv) clawback of refunded input VAGST with additional tax up to the refund amount; (v) forfeiture of the IC's tax-exempt status under s.173 of the International Companies Act 1987, exposing offshore income to 27% corporate income tax retrospectively; and (vi) regulatory action by the Registrar of International Companies against the licensed registered agent, including deregistration of the IC.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa. Supervisory and administrative authority under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Foreign Exchange Act 1975 and the Financial Institutions Act 1996. CBS licenses all Authorized Dealers (commercial banks) and administers exchange-control exemptions for International Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float linked to a basket of trading-partner currencies. Current-account transactions, including AI data-labeling service fees, BPO software subscriptions and consulting invoices from abroad, are freely convertible through Authorized Dealers without case-by-case CBS approval. Capital-account transactions, such as inbound equity subscription exceeding WST 1,000,000, cross-border loans, or China-sourced client clearing amounts, require CBS prior authorization evidenced by an Exchange Control Notification (Form EC-3). Dividend and profit remittances by a validly registered International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from surrender and repatriation requirements, and the IC may hold, retain and deploy foreign currency in external accounts provided the registered agent maintains a current UBO file and an annual licensed-agent compliance certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Domestic-flagged exporters must repatriate 100% of export proceeds to Samoa within 90 days of the date of shipment or payment, whichever is later, and surrender the proceeds to an Authorized Dealer unless an Export Retention Account (up to 50% of gross proceeds) has been approved by CBS. An International Company, once recognized as non-resident for exchange-control purposes, is expressly exempt from surrender and mandatory conversion; it is not obliged to convert USD, EUR or AUD export receipts into WST and may service all disbursements from a designated USD operational account. The exemption is conditional: no local customer sales, no securities holdings in WST, and the IC must maintain a CBS letter of non-resident status to present to its own bank and correspondents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Foreign-currency Operational Account + WST Local Payroll Sub-ledger (dual-account wrapper)
Multi-Currency Transaction Account (USD/EUR/AUD) with online treasury services
Offshore IC Savings/Operational USD Account (specialized in international-company mandates)
Corporate Operational Account (WST-led; limited multi-currency capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW to MEDIUM (restricted). Samoa has no statutory e-money institution or payment-service licensing regime; Wise, Payoneer and PayPal operate solely as unregulated-in-Samoa cross-border aggregators and cannot provide the IC with a local settlement account, IBAN-driven banking license, or CBS-recognized guarantee. Legally, an International Company must maintain its primary treasury account at a CBS-licensed Authorized Dealer; Wise and Mass_PayPal_Payout may be used only as upstream collection rails for sub-WST-100,000 client invoices, provided the EMI's statement history is unbroken and flows are mirrored to the Samoan bank. Any attempt to book the entire AI-training BPO revenue into a pure offshore EMI without an onshore operational account will fail AML due diligence at correspondent banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence at the bank branch is not mandatory for onboarding a non-resident International Company when the account is introduced by a CBS-regulated licensed registered agent or a Samoan-licensed law firm. ANZ and BSP accept a hybrid protocol: (a) remote video-KYC interview of each Director and UBO conducted by the bank's compliance officer arranged through the agent; (b) courier of notarized passports, certified board resolutions, certified amendments to the International Company Constitution, original Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; and (c) a 10-to-15-business-day enhanced due diligence review before the account go-live. A physical visit by any one Director to Apia compresses the review to approximately 5 business days. Utility bills or employer reference letters must be dated within 6 months for every UBO; Samoan-registered agent attestation letters are accepted only if the agent itself holds a financial-services license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO residency in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction, or a nominee/trust chain without a Samoa-licensed trustee making natural-person ownership opaque
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract of the Register of Members and Register of Directors; UBO organigram to ultimate natural persons with passport copies; Samoan International Trust deed listing the licensed trustee; prior-client reference from a Big-4 or CA-ANZ accountant; utility bill and bank reference not older than 6 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business classification as 'AI data labeling / RLHF' flagged by risk systems as content-moderation or IP pass-through/royalty conduit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Redacted Master Service Agreements with anonymized client identity; employment contracts for 5+ resident annotators; Apia office lease agreement; payroll summaries evidencing WST salary payments; IT asset and network topology report proving on-premise annotation workstations and VPN access logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High concentration of incoming funds from Wise or PayPal aggregator accounts instead of institutional client wires, creating unverified third-party payment exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full EMI transaction ledger with matching client invoice references; Wise for Business due-diligence and sanctions attestation; an AML/CFT compliance attestation signed by the Samoa registered agent; an internal treasury policy capping aggregator inflow at 25% of monthly revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax IC exemption triggering correspondent-bank 'shell company' screening and refusal of USD clearing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS non-resident/exchange-control exemption letter; Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour trade license; physical substance file (5+ local employees, payroll, office lease, utility bills in Samoa); board-approved economic-substance memorandum; audited financial statements prepared by a Samoan Chartered Accountant; demonstrated outward WST payroll and local VAT/tax agent filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Subscribe equity by SWIFT MT103 from the founder or holding entity with a purpose-code narrative of 'Equity Subscription - WS_IC issued share capital' mapped to BPM6 'Investment in Equity Capital'; banks route USD through correspondent Nostro accounts at Bank of New York Mellon or JPMorgan Chase New York. For capital inflows above WST 1,000,000 equivalent, submit CBS Form EC-3 via the Authorized Dealer before the wire, and attach the board resolution and UBO consent in the cover message. Service revenue from AI-training clients (data annotation, RLHF curation) is coded as BPM6 'Computer Services' with reference to the contract number; Wise collections are consolidated daily and outbound-swept to the ANZ/BSP USD account to maintain a single audit-grade ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local annotator salaries are paid in WST via BSP/ANZ domestic interbank rails (PaCS Samoa) with a monthly MT103 cover file for the bank's internal reconciliation. International AI tooling licenses (OpenAI, AWS, Hugging Face, cloud GPU providers) are settled by corporate Visa/Amex sweep from the USD account or through Wise Business on a controlled whitelist. High-value equipment and GPU server procurement above USD 50,000 must be executed via an Irrevocable at-Sight Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) opened by ANZ Samoa and reimbursed through the BNY/JPMorgan New York correspondent, with the accompanying MT103 cover payment including the LC reference number. PayPal MassPay is permitted solely for sub-threshold contractor and gig-worker payouts below USD 5,000 per beneficiary per batch and requires a monthly reconciliation statement to the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards on USD/WST solely for the defensible payroll hedge, booked with ANZ Samoa or BSP under the CBS hedging licence, with notional capped at 150% of the next 12-month projected local payroll and no speculative profit motive.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on AUD/USD and EUR/USD executed via the banks' Wellington or Sydney treasury desks, referencing announced invoice receivables from Australian and EU data-labeling clients.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) on USD/CNY permitted only when a Chinese client or RLHF sourcing counterparty pays in CNY; requires CBS capital-account prior approval and quarterly mark-to-market reporting to the Authorized Dealer.

Zero-Cost Collar (participating forward) on USD/WST extended by ANZ Samoa for the offshore payroll book where the strike collar bandwidth is limited to +/- 3% of CBS reference rate and the instrument is terminated on a rolling 6-month cycle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Government Fee Decleration (Section 118, International Companies Act 1987)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation, each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 20 per month or part thereof, up to a maximum of USD 200; continued default for 6 months after the due date may result in the Registrar issuing a notice of intention to strike off, with final strike-off and dissolution after 2 months unless cause is shown

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a Samoa International Company unless (i) shareholders holding not less than 10% of issued shares make a written request, (ii) the company is an entity licensed under a regulated activity and the licensing authority requires an audit, or (iii) the company has elected to have an audit under its constitutive documents.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Samoa, or other accounting standards expressly approved by the Registrar for International Companies; the company must keep true and fair accounts reflecting its transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent of the Samoa International Company must annually confirm, at the time the Annual Return is lodged, the accuracy of the beneficial ownership information on file, including any changes resulting from share transfers, new allotments, or changes in control. Where a shareholder transfer occurs, the register of members must be updated within a reasonable time, and the registered agent must refresh the retrospective (6-year) beneficial ownership records. Samoa's anti-money laundering framework (Financial Intelligence Unit Act) requires the agent to verify and retain UBO records for 6 years from the end of the relationship, with an annual confirmation roll-forward.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Secretaries (where a director is corporate, register of corporate directors' constituent entities)
Minute Book and Corporate Records (board and shareholder resolutions)
Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450–1,100 per annum depending on the agent and level of compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory for a standard International Company; if voluntarily engaged, a simple audit can range from USD 2,500–5,500, with a full IFRS audit at USD 6,000–10,000 depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) incorporated under Samoa's International Companies Act are exempt from all Samoa national income tax, stamp duty, estate duty, and gift duty, provided they do not derive income from Samoa sources and do not have a Samoa resident place of management. A flat annual government license fee is payable to the International Companies Registry instead of income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Report (Form IC-AR) filed with the Samoa International Companies Registry via the Government of Samoa eRegistry system. No corporate income tax return is required for an exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the annual anniversary of the date of incorporation (the Registration Anniversary Date) each year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, incorporation number, date of incorporation, registered office address in Apia, and the licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must provide the Samoa registered agent's physical address and disclose the ultimate beneficial owner's legal name, nationality, and country of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B – Share and Director Particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, share classes, and full names and addresses of all shareholders and directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and directors must supply their tax identification number and certified copy of photographic ID. Nominee appointments are permissible only if the natural beneficial owner is declared to the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C – Declaration of Exempt Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declarations that the company has not transacted business within Samoa, has no Samoa-source income, and has not created a permanent establishment in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The signatory must affirm that all data-labeling employees and servers are located outside Samoa. A board resolution stating the off-shore management location must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Samoa-licensed registered agent certifies compliance with AML/KYC file maintenance and verifies payment of the annual government license fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the registered agent's license number and electronic signature. The agent is required to retain CDD records for at least 5 years after deregistration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Report incurs a WST 300 penalty for first 30 days, followed by WST 700 for longer delays. Persistent non-filing triggers administrative strike-off and a fine up to WST 10,000 against the company, in addition to loss of legal personality.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions declared by an exempt International Company. For a Samoa tax-resident company, the statutory dividend withholding tax rate is 20%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder may claim a reduced withholding tax rate under an applicable DTA (e.g., Samoa–New Zealand) by submitting a completed Form WHT-R1 to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before the distribution, together with a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty-country tax authority and a beneficial ownership declaration. The registered agent must retain the TRC and underlying shareholder register for 6 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding rates are 15% on interest and 20% on royalties. Under the Samoa–New Zealand DTA, interest and royalty withholding may be reduced to 10%. For an exempt IC, no withholding applies on payments made by the IC to non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No transfer pricing documentation obligation is imposed on an International Company that is income-tax exempt. For a Samoa taxable resident company, a Local File and Master File are required where the aggregate annual value of controlled transactions exceeds WST 5,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations are applicable to ICs conducting relevant activities (banking, distribution, headquarters, shipping, holding, etc.). A pure AI data-labeling BPO company with no Samoa physical staffing, no local management, and no services to Samoa customers will not be treated as carrying on a relevant activity, but must file a substance declaration with the registry annually where the company is in material receipt of Samoan government tax benefits. Regular board meetings outside Samoa, sufficient overseas employees, and a clear operational nexus in a foreign jurisdiction are required to preserve the exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying the IC Annual Report declaration by concealing a physical office, employees, or servers in Samoa that generate local-source revenue from data-labeling services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015, tax evasion is punishable by a fine not exceeding WST 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years, plus an assessment of double the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, may be disqualified from serving as a director for 5 years, and travel bans may be imposed by the Ministry of Revenue pending final assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Illegal Trading after Strike-Off
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an International Company without a registered office or licensed registered agent, or continuing to transact AI outsourcing business after the Registrar has issued a strike-off notice for non-payment of annual fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa International Companies Act allows the Registrar to strike the company off the register; any subsequent contract is void and the company becomes liable to a fine up to WST 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a struck-off company who continue to operate are personally liable for all debts incurred post-strike-off and may face imprisonment of up to 5 years for fraudulent trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to receive PayPal or Wise payouts from AI training clients without conducting customer due diligence, monitoring beneficial ownership changes, or reporting suspicious transactions to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa AML/CTF Act 2018 imposes a corporate fine up to WST 2,000,000 and a natural-person officer fine up to WST 100,000 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to civil asset forfeiture, a 10-year travel ban, and imprisonment up to 7 years for laundering money derived from foreign criminal conduct, notwithstanding the company's corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Offshore Management and Permanent Establishment Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors physically present in Samoa who exercise executive control over the data-labeling workforce, while the company continues to claim the IC tax exemption and avoids registering a Samoa branch.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A permanent establishment in Samoa is deemed to exist, exposing the company to Samoa corporate income tax at 27% on attributable profits, plus late payment penalties of 20% per annum and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Non-resident directors found to have managed the IC from Samoa are personally assessed to the unpaid tax and may be subjected to freezing orders on Samoa bank accounts and civil restitution of distributed sums.
